sections.title: 3. Travel Grammar: Past Experiences
sections.description: Using past tenses effectively to describe travel experiences and memories.

points.title: Past Simple for Completed Actions
points.function: To describe completed travel experiences in chronological order
examples: I visited the Eiffel Tower last summer.
We stayed in a boutique hotel in Paris.

points.title: Past Continuous for Background Actions
points.function: To describe ongoing actions during which something else happened
examples: I was taking photos when the sun set behind the mountains.
They were exploring the market when they found the antique shop.

points.title: Present Perfect for Recent Experiences
points.function: To describe travel experiences that have relevance to the present
examples: I have traveled to over 15 countries.
She has never experienced such breathtaking scenery before.

rows: I visited three museums during my trip.
We were hiking when it started to rain.
I have explored many European cities.

tip.title: Pro-Tip: Tense Clarity
tip.text: Use past simple for specific completed trips, and present perfect for general travel experiences that may continue.

sections.title: Travel Vocabulary Practice
sections.description: Choose the best word or phrase to complete each travel sentence.

questions.prompt: "The ________ views from the mountain top were absolutely stunning."
questions.explanation: Breathtaking describes scenery so impressive that it leaves a strong emotional reaction; boring and tiring describe different experiences.

questions.prompt: "To truly understand a culture, you need to experience ________ with the local community."
questions.explanation: Cultural immersion involves close participation in local life; shopping malls and fast food do not provide that depth of experience.

questions.prompt: "We decided to explore ________ areas instead of popular tourist destinations."
questions.explanation: Off the beaten path is the fixed expression for places away from common tourist routes; the other phrases are not idiomatic.

questions.prompt: "________ focuses on minimizing environmental impact and supporting local communities."
questions.explanation: Sustainable tourism aims to limit environmental harm and benefit local communities; luxury and budget describe cost or style.

questions.prompt: "One of the highlights of my trip was trying the local ________ at traditional restaurants."
questions.explanation: Local cuisine means the food and cooking tradition of a place; menu is a list of dishes and waiter is a person.

questions.prompt: "Before our vacation, we spent weeks planning our travel ________."
questions.explanation: A travel itinerary is the planned sequence of places and activities; insurance and passport are travel documents, not the plan.

questions.prompt: "The hotel was a charming boutique ________ with excellent service."
questions.explanation: Establishment can formally refer to a hotel or business; airport and restaurant identify different types of place.

questions.prompt: "During our ________, we discovered a hidden waterfall in the jungle."
questions.explanation: Adventure describes an unusual, exciting experience such as discovering a waterfall; homework and meeting do not fit the journey context.

questions.prompt: "The village was so ________ that it looked like it was from another century."
questions.explanation: Picturesque describes an attractively old-fashioned scene; expensive and crowded concern cost or population rather than appearance.

questions.prompt: "Even years later, everyone in our group still talks about the trip because it was an ________ experience."
questions.explanation: Unforgettable means impossible to forget and matches the fact that the group still discusses the trip years later.

sections.title: Listening: Resolving a Hotel Complaint
sections.description: Listen for the guest's priorities and evaluate the proposed resolution.

audio.transcript: Good evening. I'm calling from room four twelve. I booked a quiet room because I have an early flight, but there's a wedding reception directly below me. I understand the music is scheduled to continue until midnight. I'm very sorry. The reception was moved at short notice because another room developed a plumbing problem. We can move you to room six thirty, which is on the opposite side of the building. Is that room available now? I need to sleep soon, and I don't want to wait while it is prepared. It was cleaned this afternoon, so a colleague can bring a new key within five minutes. The room is smaller, but it has been upgraded with breakfast and a late checkout. The breakfast won't help because I leave before it opens. Could you arrange a taxi and a takeaway breakfast instead? Yes, we can book a taxi for five fifteen and prepare a breakfast bag. I'll also remove tonight's parking charge. That sounds reasonable. Please confirm the arrangements by text so I have the times in writing. Of course. You'll receive the message shortly, and the duty manager will call after you move to ensure the new room is quiet.

gistQuestions.prompt: What outcome do the speakers reach?
options: The guest moves rooms and receives practical alternatives
gistQuestions.explanation: They agree on a quieter room, taxi, breakfast bag and removed parking charge.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why is the original room noisy?
detailQuestions.explanation: The wedding reception is directly below the room.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why does the guest reject the normal breakfast?
options: The flight requires an earlier departure
detailQuestions.explanation: The guest leaves before breakfast opens.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: In service encounters, distinguish the original complaint, constraints, rejected offers and final agreement.

sections.title: Writing Part 4: Travel Experience
sections.description: Write a short formal response using the vocabulary from this lesson.

prompt.situation: You have been asked to write a short article for your school magazine about an unforgettable travel experience. Describe where you went, what you did, and why it was memorable. Use at least 5 vocabulary words from this lesson.
prompt.referenceAnswer: Last summer, I had the opportunity to experience cultural immersion in a picturesque village in Vietnam. The breathtaking scenery and warm hospitality of the locals made this an unforgettable adventure. I explored off the beaten path locations and tried the delicious local cuisine. This sustainable tourism experience taught me the importance of respecting local communities while traveling. It was truly a memorable journey that broadened my perspective on different cultures.

tip.title: B2 Writing Tip
tip.text: Use a variety of past tenses to make your travel narrative more engaging. Combine past simple for completed actions with past continuous for ongoing experiences.
